record.context_brief: Uniform random generation of fullerene isomers
record.original_question: A fullerene is a convex, 3-regular polytope consisting only of pentagonal and hexagonal facets. For a feasible integer n, meaning a positive even integer n >= 20 with n != 22, let C_n denote the set of all fullerenes with exactly n vertices, considered up to graph isomorphism as fullerene isomers. Can one design a computationally efficient procedure that samples uniformly from the fullerene isomers in C_n, so that every isomer in C_n is selected with the same probability?

evidence.quote: A fullerene is a convex, 3-regular polytope consisting only of pentagonal and hexagonal facets.
Thus, we define a positive even integer n ≥ 20, n ̸= 22, as feasible.
Let Cn denote the set of all fullerenes with exactly n vertices. This set can be partitioned into equivalence classes under graph isomorphisms, with each class referred to as a Cn -isomer.
Open Problem 1. Develop a computationally efficient algorithm to generate a uniform distribution on fullerene isomers Cn for all feasible n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A fullerene is a convex 3-regular polytope whose facets are all pentagons or hexagons; equivalently (via its 1-skeleton), a 3-regular planar graph all of whose faces have length 5 or 6. By Euler's formula such a graph must have exactly 12 pentagonal faces, and the number n of vertices satisfies: n is even, n ≥ 20, and n ≠ 22. Call such an integer n feasible. For each feasible n, let C_n denote the set of all fullerenes with exactly n vertices, considered up to graph isomorphism (i.e., the equivalence classes are the C_n-isomers).

Design a computationally efficient algorithm (running in time polynomial in n, or otherwise demonstrably tractable) that, for any feasible input n, outputs a fullerene isomer in C_n drawn uniformly at random — i.e., such that every isomorphism class in C_n is produced with probability exactly 1/|C_n|.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of efficiently generating fullerene isomers uniformly at random is stated as an open problem. Existing algorithms (face spiral, growth/Stone–Wales operations, Buckygen) can enumerate fullerenes — Buckygen being the fastest known full enumerator — but exhaustive enumeration becomes infeasible for large n (e.g., n > 400) due to the rapid growth of |C_n|, and no known efficient algorithm samples uniformly from C_n for all feasible n.

status_evidence.title: The Generation of Fullerenes (Buckygen)
status_evidence.snippet: Buckygen is up to now the fastest algorithm to generate all Cn-isomers, but enumeration becomes computationally prohibitive for large n.
status_evidence.claim: State-of-the-art enumeration is exhaustive; no efficient uniform sampler is known.

status_evidence.title: Spectral clustering of combinatorial fullerene isomers
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses fullerene isomer enumeration and structural properties; uniform random generation remains a noted challenge.
status_evidence.claim: Uniform random generation of fullerene isomers is recognized as not solved by current methods.
